fields.narrative_intro: *A skittish person and a flustered person discuss GPT-6 Astra inside a broken time machine stuck between two eras.*
fields.panel1:
[setup]
SKITTISH PERSON: "Today's headline: GPT-6 Astra."
[Visual: They hold a newspaper whose entire story is one ominous URL.]
fields.panel2:
[build]
FLUSTERED PERSON: "Excellent. What can Astra do?"
[Visual: The time machine's future dial spins wildly while its screen displays OPENAI.COM.]
fields.panel3:
[pivot]
SKITTISH PERSON: "HTTP 403: the article won't let us find out."
[Visual: A tiny velvet rope labeled 403 blocks the time machine's information console.]
fields.panel4:
[silent reaction]
[Visual: Both stare at a locked glass display labeled GPT-6 Astra; inside, a blank newspaper floats.]
fields.panel5:
[punch]
FLUSTERED PERSON: "So it's advanced enough to deny journalism?"
SKITTISH PERSON: "Apparently, from both eras."
fields.panel6:
[button]
[Visual: The machine's output slot prints 403 Forbidden into yesterday, tomorrow, and every blank edition. ]

narrative_summary: GPT-6 Astra remains unknowable because OpenAI's HTTP 403 has become the only information successfully traveling through time.
rationale: Candidate 5 makes the 403 blockage visually specific and turns it into a credible AI-capability joke: Astra is advanced enough to deny journalism across time. The other pitches mostly repeat that the article is inaccessible, while Candidate 5 gives the premise a stronger sight-gag structure and cleaner closing beat.
place: inside a broken time machine stuck between two eras
hat_pair: foam diploma scroll worn as a top hat with a tiny tassel dangling off
crash helmet with a tiny working traffic light mounted on top
